THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 3, 1937

"BLOOD ALLEY" CLASH
UP IN COMMONS

Fight Between British
Soldiers, Italian
Bluejackets

EDEN SAYS INCIDENT
SETTLED AMICABLY

LONDON, March 1.—The recent
clash between Italian sailors and
British soldiers in a cabaret on Rue
Chu Pao San, Shanghai, known
locally as "Blood Alley," was dis-
cussed in the House of Commons to-
day.

The subject was raised by Mr. W.
A. Burke, Labour Member for
Burnley, who asked whether the
attention of the Foreign Secretary,
Mr. Anthony Eden, had been drawn
to the attack by Italian naval men
on soldiers belonging to the Loyal
North Lancashire Regiment, and
whether he proposed to make repre-
sentations to the Italian Government
on the matter.

Replying, Mr. Eden detailed the
affair.
"I understand," he added, "that
the incident has been amicably
settled by the respective command-
ers. Italian sailors visited the in-
jured Britons in hospital with pre-
sents, and are inviting a party of
British troops to an entertainment
aboard their gunboat. The last part
of the question, therefore, does not
appear to arise."—Reuter.

Outcome Of Isis Fray

The clash referred to above took
place on Sunday night, February 21,
and was attributed to a squabble over
a woman which culminated in hot re-
marks being passed by the Britons over
the alleged poor sportsmanship of the
Italians who wrecked the Isis Theatre
the night previously. Battle began
with a few men in one cabaret but
soon spread the length of the cabaret
street, involving some 60 men.
Bars and various other weapons be-
side fists were employed in the fight,
with the result that three British
soldiers suffered painful injuries and
had to be confined to hospital. The
fight was finally broken up by French
Police in co-operation with military
police squads.

RUE CHU PAO SAN IN
THE LIMELIGHT

We have it on the authority of Holy
Writ that "evil communications corrupt
good manners" but sometimes we are
almost led to the belief that rapid
communications are injurious to com-
monsense. Thus, the matter of the clash
between Italian sailors and British
soldiers a few days ago in a cabaret in
the Rue Chu Pao San at Shanghai, some-
times referred to as "Blood Alley," was
raised in the House of Commons on
Monday by Mr. W. A. Burke, Labour
Member for Burnley, who wanted to
know, inter alia, whether the Foreign
Secretary proposed to make representa-
tions to the Italian Government on the
incident. Fortunately, Mr. Eden was
able to reply that he understood that the
incident had been amicably settled by the
respective commanders. Italians sailors
had visited the injured Britons in hospital
with presents, and were inviting a party
of British troops to an entertainment
aboard their gunboat. The last part of
Mr. Burke's question, that is to say, with
reference to making representations to
the Italian Government, therefore did
not appear to arise. This local settlement
is, of course, just what should be, and
we do not believe for a moment that the
slightest political significance arises in
such a cabaret incident. Such isolated
incidents will arise from time to time and
their settlement by the local commanding
officers is the proper way to deal with
them. If there had been any suggestion
of constant serious friction between the
armed forces of Britain and Italy in
Shanghai, or any other port, it might have
been necessary to make it a question for
Governments to consider but happily this
is not the case.

“血巷”冲突
引发下议院讨论

英军士兵与意大利水兵发生斗殴

艾登称事件已友好解决

伦敦，3月1日电。——近日，意大利水兵与英国士兵在上海朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San，当地俗称“血巷”）的一家歌舞厅内发生冲突，此事今日在英国下议院进行讨论。

该议题由伯恩利选区工党议员W. A. 伯克先生提出，他询问外交大臣安东尼·艾登先生是否已注意到意大利海军人员袭击隶属于皇家北兰开夏团（Loyal North Lancashire Regiment）士兵一事，以及他是否打算就此向意大利政府提出交涉。

艾登先生在答复中详细说明了此事经过。
他补充说：“据我了解，该事件已由双方指挥官友好解决。意大利水兵携带礼物前往医院探望受伤的英国人，并邀请一队英国官兵到其炮舰上参加娱乐活动。因此，问题的最后一部分似乎已不成立。”——路透社。

伊西斯剧院斗殴事件的后果

上述冲突发生在2月21日（星期日）晚间，起因是争风吃醋，最终演变为激烈口角。英国人指责意大利人在前一晚捣毁伊西斯剧院（Isis Theatre）的行为缺乏体育精神。战斗始于一家歌舞厅内的几人之间，但很快蔓延至整条歌舞厅街道，卷入人数约60人。打斗中除了拳脚外，还使用了酒吧器具及其他各种武器，导致三名英国士兵受重伤并不得不留院治疗。这场斗殴最终在法国警察与宪兵分队的合作下被平息。

朱葆三路成为焦点

圣经有云：“不良的交往败坏良好的品行”，但有时我们几乎要相信，快速的通讯有害于常识。因此，几天前上海朱葆三路（有时被称为“血巷”）一家歌舞厅内意大利水兵与英国士兵之间的冲突事件，于周一在下议院被伯恩利选区工党议员W. A. 伯克先生提起，他想了解，除其他事项外，外交大臣是否打算就此事件向意大利政府提出交涉。幸运的是，艾登先生能够回答说，据他了解，该事件已由双方指挥官友好解决。意大利水兵已携带礼物前往医院探望受伤的英国人，并邀请一队英国官兵到其炮舰上参加娱乐活动。因此，伯克先生问题的最后一部分，即关于向意大利政府提出交涉的部分，似乎已不成立。这种本地化的解决方式当然是应有的做法，我们丝毫不认为此类歌舞厅事件具有任何政治意义。此类孤立事件会不时发生，由当地指挥官进行处理是适当的解决方式。如果英国和意大利武装部队在上海或其他港口存在持续严重摩擦的迹象，可能有必要将其作为由政府考虑的问题，但幸运的是情况并非如此。

SUNDAY'S INCIDENT
AMICABLY CLOSED

Italian, British Authorities
in Agreement

Yesterday a conference between
the British and Italian authorities
took place and it was agreed that
the unfortunate clash on Sunday
night between men of the Loyal
Regiment and naval ratings from
the Italian gunboat Lepanto was the
outcome of the previous evening's
disturbance. So far as could be
ascertained by the authorities, the
number of Italian sailors involved
was not more than twelve, the
British soldiers being six in number,
although it was possible that other
parties became involved.

Both parties agreed that there
was no fighting in the street. As a
result of these investigations, the
Brigadier of the British Military
Forces and the Italian Naval Com-
mander considered that the incident
was amicably closed.

Yesterday morning, an officer of
the Lepanto, accompanied by six
Italian sailors, paid a friendly visit
to the British Military Hospital, 24
Central Road, where the two injured
men were being treated, and left
flowers and sweetmeats with message
of sympathetic enquiry. The two
soldiers are expected to leave the
hospital by the end of the week.

farther end of the hall, I ran to that place followed by
S.I. Manneville, and saw another Italian sailor armed with
a big piece of wood, who endeavoured to penetrate into
the lavatories where 2 British soldiers who had already
been wounded, took a refuge. Upon being seized by S.I.
Manneville, the sailor immediately turned round and was
about to hit with his club when, upon an order shouted
by the man in charge of the Italian patrol, he stopped.
I ordered two policemen to clear the dancing hall with the
assistance of the patrols, leaving in the place only the
wounded British soldiers, the dancing partners and the
American sailors. At the time when the hall was being
cleared another small incident took place: the manager
of the establishment received several blows of fist from
an Italian sailor and the Police and the Italian patrol
had again to intervene. The man in charge of the Italian
patrol ordered his men to board an Italian Navy truck
which was stationed in the Rue Chu Pao San in order to
send them on board their ship. The man in charge of the
British patrol got their wounded men together at the
Lazare Bar, after which they were taken to the hospital
in an ambulance. It should be noted that at the time the
Police and the patrols intervened at the Charleston Cafe,
there were in the place only 6 or 7 British soldiers, about
10 Italian sailors, and 3 or 4 American sailors (who did
not take part in the fighting) and the personnel of the
establishment.

Dear General,

I have the honour to inform you that on Saturday 20th and Sunday 21st February several rows took place in different dancing haunts in CHU PAO SAN ROAD between Italian Marines and British soldiers.

What took place at the Charleston Cafe on Saturday did not appear to be very serious and only amounted to a few blows. Order was immediately restored on the arrival of the French Police and the English and Italian Patrols.

The incidents on Sunday night were more serious. After two incidents of no importance at the Frisco Cabaret, a much more serious one developed at the Charleston Cafe about 10.p.m. At the time when the Police, followed by the English and Italian Patrols entered the Cafe a veritable battle was going on between 5 or 6 Italian Marines and about an equal number of British soldiers. It appeared that at least two of the Italian Marines used large sticks to hit the English soldiers with. Five English soldiers had been more or less wounded, three of them had been sent to Hospital. At the moment when the Police, assisted by the Patrols, emptied the Cafe, an Italian hit the Manager of the Charleston. He was almost immediately hauled away by the Commander of the Italian Patrol. After these incidents the man i/c Italian Patrol ordered his men to get into a bus which was awaiting them, and saw them all in. The five wounded English soldiers were, at the command of the man in charge of their Patrol, sent to Hospital in an ambulance.

We do not know what the origin was of the argument which rapidly developed into a fight. We do not propose to find out. We must draw certain conclusions from from the incident, to which I would respectfully draw your attention.

In the first place, the Military Patrols, as a matter of fact, give excellent results when they are concerned with taking slightly drunk soldiers back to Barracks, but they are not much use for intervening in more serious rows because they too easily take sides for their own nationals, which after all is only human, but the row will thus become more serious.

The only answer would be, if we fear the recurrence of such incidents, to organize mixed Patrols composed of picked Police and M.C.Os of each nationality.

I should be very grateful if you would give me your opinion of this formula for complete neutrality.

A second.....

尊敬的将军：

本人谨荣幸地告知您，2月20日（星期六）和21日（星期日），在朱葆三路的不同跳舞场所，意大利海军陆战队员与英国士兵之间发生了数起争吵。

周六在查尔斯顿咖啡馆发生的事件似乎并不十分严重，仅止于几次拳脚相加。随着法国警方以及英国和意大利巡逻队的到达，秩序立即得到恢复。

周日夜间的事件更为严重。在弗里斯科歌舞厅发生两起无关紧要的小冲突后，晚上约10时，查尔斯顿咖啡馆发生了一起更为严重的斗殴。当警方在英国和意大利巡逻队的紧随下进入咖啡馆时，五或六名意大利海军陆战队员与大致同等数量的英国士兵之间正在进行一场真正的搏斗。看来至少有两名为意大利海军陆战队员使用大棍棒殴打英国士兵。五名英国士兵受到不同程度的伤害，其中三人已被送往医院。当警方在巡逻队协助下清空咖啡馆时，一名意大利人击打了查尔斯顿咖啡馆的经理。他几乎立即被意大利巡逻队指挥官带走。在这些事件之后，意大利巡逻队负责人命令其手下进入一辆等候他们的巴士，并看着他们全部上车。五名受伤的英国士兵在其巡逻队负责人的命令下，由救护车送往医院。

我们不知道这场迅速演变为斗殴的争吵起因何在。我们不打算去查明。我们必须从这一事件中得出某些结论，对此我谨提请阁下注意。

首先，军事巡逻队在护送略微醉酒的士兵回营房方面确实效果良好，但在干预更严重的争吵方面作用不大，因为他们太容易偏袒本国国民，这毕竟是人情之常，但这会使争吵变得更加严重。

如果我们担心此类事件再次发生，唯一的解决办法就是组织混合巡逻队，由各国精选的警察和军事宪警军官组成。

如蒙阁下对这种完全中立的方案赐示高见，本人将不胜感激。

我们并不知晓这场迅速演变为斗殴的争执之起因。我们也无意探究其原因。但我们必须从这一事件中吸取教训，谨此荣幸地提请阁下注意。

首先，目前的军事巡逻队在遣返情绪稍显激动的士兵回营房方面成效显著，但在介入斗殴时却作用有限，因为他们太容易——这也是人之常情——偏袒本国同胞。这反而使事态更加严重。唯一的补救办法在于

lorsque nous craignons des incidents, d'organiser des

de sous-officiers de chaque nationalité. Je vous serais
reconnaissant de me donner votre opinion sur cette formule

Une deuxième conclusion s'impose, c'est qu'il
est absolument indispensable, dans des cas comme celui-ci,
de donner à la discipline une force supérieure à celle de
l'échauffement des esprits, même si ce dernier est justi-
fié. Cela évitera de faire jouer à notre Police un rôle
profondément ingrat, rôle qu'elle n'assume que lorsqu'elle
y est contrainte, et qu'elle préférerait voir remplacer
par un esprit de camaraderie internationale qu'ici nous
désirons de toutes nos forces. Mais ce résultat ne peut
être réalisé que par une entente entre les divers comman-
dements.

En vous demandant de me donner votre avis sur
ces suggestions, qui n'ont d'autre but que de mettre fin à
des dissentiments regrettables et de maintenir l'ordre
public dans les quartiers fréquentés par les militaires de
toutes nationalités, veuillez agréer, Mon Général, l'assu-
rance de mes sentiments les plus respectueux./.

第二个必然得出的结论是，在此类情况下，绝对必须使纪律的力量压倒情绪的激动，即便后者有其正当理由。这将避免让我们的警察扮演极不讨好的角色；他们只有在被迫时才承担这一角色，而我们在此极力希望以国际友爱精神取而代之。但这一结果只有通过各指挥部门之间的协调才能实现。

To :-

Sir,
    I have to report for your information that
at SHANGHAI on the 21st February, 1937, about 10-25 p.m.
I was on duty in RUE CHUA POA SAN where I was called
into the CHARLSTON CABARET.
    I went in and a disturbance was taking place
between Italian Sailors and British Troops, several
of the Italian Sailors had pieces of piping in their
hands.
    Five English soldiers were lying on the floor
one of the soldiers was bleeding profusely from the head.
    I immediately ordered all the British soldiers to
leave the cabaret and with the assistance of my patrol
all the injured were taken to the Cosy Corner Cafe, were
I rendered first aid, pending the arrival of the
ambulance.
    The five soldiers were taken to hospital. Ptes
Bennett, Pomfret and Robinson of the 2nd. Bn. The Loyal
Regiment were detained. Ptes Heathcote and Brayshaw
were allowed to proceed to their barracks.

                        (sgd) R. THOMAS. Cpl.

Shanghai,
22/2/37.                Corps of Military Police.

Statement made by No. 365879 Pte. Heathcote E. Fnd.Mn. The Loyal
Regiment.

On the 21st.February 1937 at about 10.15 p.m. I entered
the Charleston Cabaret, Rue Chua Pon San.

At about 10.30 p.m. I was sitting at a table watching my
friends, Privates Bonfret, Dragshaw and Robinson, dancing.

Suddenly about twenty(20) Italians (I recognised them by
their uniforms) entered the Cabaret and set about all present,
concentrating their efforts on the British Troops.

One Italian approached me and struck me on the arm and in
self defence I knocked him over on to the floor with a chair.

I was able to keep the Italians at bay until the arrival
of the Military and Civil Police.

(Sd). E. HEATHCOTE, Pte.

Taken down by me on the 22nd.February 1937.

(Sd). C. SMITH, Lieut.
Fnd.Mn. The Loyal Regt.
pages.zh:
忠诚团步兵（Fnd.Mn. The Loyal Regiment）编号 365879 二等兵 Heathcote E. 所作陈述。

1937年2月21日晚10时15分左右，我进入位于朱葆三街（Rue Chua Pon San）的查尔斯顿歌舞厅。

晚10时30分左右，我坐在桌旁，看着我的朋友 Bonfret、Dragshaw 和 Robinson 二等兵跳舞。

突然，大约二十（20）名意大利人（我从他们的制服认出他们）进入歌舞厅，袭击在场所有人，并将矛头集中在英国部队身上。

一名意大利人走近我，击打我的手臂，出于自卫，我用一把椅子将他打倒在地。

在军方和民间警察到达之前，我一直能够抵挡住意大利人。

（签名）E. HEATHCOTE，二等兵。

由我于1937年2月22日记录。

（签名）C. SMITH，中尉。
忠诚团步兵。

pages.en:
Statement made by No. 955104 Pte. F. BRADSHAW, 2nd Bn. The Loyal Regt.

On the 21st. February 1937 I visited the Charleston Cabaret
Rue Chua Pou San at bout 10.3 p.m. I was with Privates Pomfret,
Robinson and Heathcote, of the 2nd Bn. The Loyal Regiment.

A crowd of Italian Sailors (I recognised them by their Italian
uniforms) were sitting on the far side of the Dance Hall. Pte.
Pomfret and I got up to dance and it was then that I saw one of the
Italians strike Pte. Robinson for no apparent reason .

This sailor was soon joined by what appeared to be a Patrol
of Italian Sailors armed with batons.

They set about all British Soldiers present (about seven of us)
I myself was struck on the head and the elbow. In self defence I
tried to protect myself by using a chair.

In a short time the trouble was stopped by Military and Civil
Policemen.

(Sd). F. BRADSHAW, Pte.

Taken down in my presence on 22nd. February 1937.

(Sd). C. Smith Lieut.
2nd Bn. The Loyal Regt.
pages.zh:
忠诚团第2营编号 955104 二等兵 F. BRADSHAW 所作陈述。

1937年2月21日晚10时03分左右，我访问了位于朱葆三街（Rue Chua Pou San）的查尔斯顿歌舞厅。我与忠诚团第2营的 Pomfret、Robinson 和 Heathcote 二等兵在一起。

一群意大利水兵（我从他们的意大利制服认出他们）坐在舞厅的另一侧。Pomfret 二等兵和我起身跳舞，就在这时，我看见一名意大利人毫无明显理由地击打了 Robinson 二等兵。

这名水兵很快得到了一支援军的加入，这似乎是一支装备棍棒的意大利水兵巡逻队。

他们袭击了在场的所有英国士兵（我们大约七人）。我本人头部和肘部受到击打。出于自卫，我试图用椅子保护自己。

不久，军方和民间警察制止了骚乱。

（签名）F. BRADSHAW，二等兵。

1937年2月22日在我面前记录。

（签名）C. Smith 中尉。
忠诚团第2营。

Statement made by No. 3854798 Pte Bound C.
2nd Bn. The Loyal Regiment.
------------------------------------------------------------

On 21st February 1937 at about 7.45.p.m. I
entered the CHARLESTON CABARET, Rue CHAO PAC SAN,
in company with Pte Bennett.

At about 10.p.m. I was watching my friends
dancing when suddenly a large crowd of Italians
rushed into the Cabaret and set about the British
troops (who seem to be the only men present) with
batons.

The sudden attack was quite unexpected and
beyond my apprehension.

I was attacked and before I could protect
myself I was practically knocked out by a blow
in the ribs and head.

As I was getting up to go for help the Police
arrived on the scene.

(sd) C. BOUND. Pte.

Taken down on 22nd February, 1937 by Lieut C.J. Smith,
2/Loyal Regt.
pages.zh:
忠诚团第2营编号 3854798 二等兵 Bound C. 所作陈述。
---

1937年2月21日晚7时45分左右，我
与 Bennett 二等兵一起进入位于赵家浜路（Rue CHAO PAC SAN）的查尔斯顿歌舞厅（CHARLESTON CABARET）。

晚10时左右，我正在观看朋友
跳舞，突然一大群意大利人
冲进歌舞厅，用棍棒袭击英国
部队（他们似乎是当时在场的唯一人员）。

这次突然袭击完全出乎意料，
超出了我的预料。

我遭到攻击，在我能够保护自己
之前，我的肋骨和头部受到重击，
几乎被打昏。

当我起身去寻求帮助时，警察
到达了现场。

（签名）C. BOUND，二等兵。

由忠诚团第2营 C.J. Smith 中尉
于1937年2月22日记录。

pages.en:
No.3853994 Pte. Orchard A., 2nd Bn. The Loyal Regiment states:-

At Shanghai on the 20/2/1937 I was in the Charleston Cabaret
in Rue Chua Poa San with about five other British Soldiers; there
were also in the Cabaret about eighteen Italian Sailers sitting on
the opposite side of the dance floor.

At aproximately 9.30 p.m. there was one British Soldier and
one Italion Sailor only dancing on the dance floor. The Etalion
suddenly struck at the British Soldier dancing for no apparent
reason. As this happened all the other Italions suddenly got up
and rushed across the floor at us yelling and shouting and throwing
chairs and tables at us.

The British Police Corporal and Two G.M.Ps. tried to stop the
Italions but were unable to and the Police Corporal got knocked out
in trying to do so. The Italion Police also interferred and
order was eventually restored.

All the Italions were ordered out of the Cabaret. When
they had gone out all my friends went to the latrine and I was left
in the Cabaret by myself.

Suddenly I saw four Italions inside the Cabaret coming to-
wards me and at the same time I saw the remainder of the Italions
coming back in.

They went for me and I don't remember clearly what happened
until I was told to get up as all was quiet again.

(Sd). A. W. ORCHARD, Pte.

Taken down at Shanghai on the 22/2/1937 by Lieut. E. H.
Leschallas, 2nd Bn. The Loyal Regiment.

(Sd). E.H.LESCHALLAS, Lieut.
pages.zh:
忠诚团第2营编号 3853994 二等兵 Orchard A. 陈述如下：

1937年2月20日，在上海，我和其他大约五名英国士兵一起在朱葆三街（Rue Chua Poa San）的查尔斯顿歌舞厅；歌舞厅里还有大约十八名意大利水手坐在舞池对面。

晚上9时30分左右，舞池上只有一名英国士兵和一名意大利水手在跳舞。那名意大利人突然毫无明显理由地击打了正在跳舞的英国士兵。随着这一事件的发生，所有其他意大利人突然起身，向我们冲过舞池，叫喊喧哗，并向我们投掷椅子和桌子。

英国警长和两名宪兵（G.M.Ps.）试图阻止意大利人，但未能成功，警长在试图阻止时被打昏。意大利警察也介入干预，秩序最终得以恢复。

所有意大利人被勒令离开歌舞厅。当他们出去后，我的朋友们都去了洗手间，留下我一个人在歌舞厅里。

突然，我看见四名意大利人在歌舞厅内向我走来，同时我看见其余的意大利人正返回进来。

他们向我扑来，直到有人叫我起来，因为一切又安静下来之前，我不清楚记得发生了什么。

（签名）A. W. ORCHARD，二等兵。

由忠诚团第2营 E. H. Leschallas 中尉
于1937年2月22日在上海记录。

（签名）E.H.LESCHALLAS，中尉。

pages.en:
No. 3445190 Pte. Vesty, W., Pnd.mn. The Loyal Regiment states:-

At Shanghai on the 20/9/1937 I was in the Charleston
Cabaret in the Rue Chua Foa San with about five other British Soldiers
At approximately 9.30 p.m. there was one British Soldier
dancing and one Italian dancing on the dance floor; on the other
side of the room there were about eighteen Italian Sailors sitting
down at tables.

The Italian who was dancing suddenly struck at the
British Soldier dancing for no apparent reason whatsoever as far as
I could see.

At the same time all the Italian Sailors who were sitting
at the other side of the room came across the dance floor towards
the British Soldiers, shouting and yelling and started to throw
chairs and tables at the British.

The British Police Corporal and two J.M.P's tried to
interfere, but the Corporal was knocked out. The Italian Police
also came in and order was eventually restored.

All the Italians were ordered out of the Cabaret. I then
went off to the latrine with about three or four other British
Soldiers. There was one Italian in the latrine who immediately
started arguing.

The Italian then walked out of the latrine by himself.
I followed out soon after and I saw four Italians going towards
Private Orchard who was by himself with obvious intent to hurt him.

At the same time all the other Italians came back into
the Cabaret and then another rough house started.

I, then, found myself in the middle of the riot, on the
floor with several Italians over me.

I don't remember anything else until I was picked up
outside by a Military Policeman and sent to a nearby Police Station
where they took my particulars.

(Sd). W. VESTY, Pte.

Taken down at Shanghai on 20/9/1937 by Lieut. E. H.
Leschallas, Pnd.mn. The Loyal Regiment.

(Sd). E. H. Leschallas, Lieut.,
pages.zh:
忠诚团步兵（Pnd.mn. The Loyal Regiment）编号 3445190 二等兵 Vesty, W. 陈述如下：

1937年9月20日，在上海，我和其他大约五名英国士兵一起在朱葆三街（Rue Chua Foa San）的查尔斯顿歌舞厅。晚上9时30分左右，舞池上有一名英国士兵和一名意大利人在跳舞；房间的另一侧大约有十八名意大利水手坐在桌旁。

据我所见，正在跳舞的那名意大利人突然毫无任何明显理由地击打了正在跳舞的英国士兵。

与此同时，所有坐在房间另一侧的意大利水手穿过舞池冲向英国士兵，叫喊喧哗，并开始向英国人投掷椅子和桌子。

英国警长和两名宪兵（J.M.P's）试图干预，但警长被打昏。意大利警察也进入现场，秩序最终得以恢复。

所有意大利人被勒令离开歌舞厅。随后，我和其他大约三四名英国士兵去了洗手间。洗手间里有一名意大利人，他立即开始争吵。

随后那名意大利人独自走出洗手间。我不久后也跟了出去，看见四名意大利人走向独自一人的 Orchard 二等兵，显然意图伤害他。

与此同时，所有其他意大利人返回歌舞厅，接着又开始了另一次斗殴。

随后，我发现自己身处骚乱中心，倒在地上，几名意大利人压在我身上。

除此之外我不记得任何其他事情，直到我被一名宪兵从外面扶起，并被送到附近的警察局，在那里他们登记了我的个人信息。

（签名）W. VESTY，二等兵。

由忠诚团步兵 E. H. Leschallas 中尉
于1937年9月20日在上海记录。

（签名）E. H. Leschallas，中尉，

pages.en:
Statement by No, 3852024 Corporal D.M. CROWIN,
2nd. Bn. The Loyal Regiment.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

On 21st February, 1957, at about 10.p.m. I
was in the Frisco Cabaret (corner of RUK CHU POA SAN and
AVENUE EDWARD VII). I was dancing on the dance floor.
There were only two couples. The other man was an
Italian sailor. As we were dancing we brushed against
each other. It was an accident. I made no attempt to
touch him. I turned round to apologise, but before I had
time to do so he struck me on the jaw and the mouth with
his fist. He struck me about three times, and I fell to
the ground. The attack was so sudden that I did not have
time to defend myself. While I was picking myself up (I
was in a dazed condition) I saw him run to pick up a
chair. He picked the chair up, but at that moment the
Italian Naval Patrol interfered and stopped him. I walked
back to my seat.

When this incident happened it was the first
time I had noticed this Italian. I had done nothing to
provoke him, or any other Italian.

I was accompanied in the Frisco Cabaret by
two Bandsmen [Bandsmen Gerrity and Broomhead). I had
left them to dance, and as we were occupying a table
in the corner they did not witness the incident.

(sd) D.M. CROWIN. Corpl.

Taken down by me on 22nd February, 1957.

22.2.57.
Lieut.
D.A.P.M.
pages.zh:
第3852024号下士 D.M. CROWIN 的陈述，
忠诚团（The Loyal Regiment）第二营。
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

1957年2月21日，晚上约10点，我
在弗里斯科歌舞厅（Frisco Cabaret）（位于RUK CHU POA SAN街与
爱德华七世大道（AVENUE EDWARD VII）转角处）。我正在舞池里跳舞。
当时只有两对舞伴。另一名男子是一名
意大利水手。我们在跳舞时互相擦碰。
这是一次意外。我并未试图触碰他。我转身准备道歉，但还没来得及
这样做，他就用拳头击打我的下巴和嘴部。他大约打了三拳，我倒在地上。
袭击来得如此突然，以至于我没有时间自卫。当我挣扎着站起来时（我
处于神志不清的状态），我看见他跑过去拿起一把椅子。他拿起了椅子，但就在那一刻，
意大利海军巡逻队介入并制止了他。我走回自己的座位。

当此事发生时，是我第一次注意到这名意大利人。我并没有做任何事情去
挑衅他，或任何其他意大利人。

在弗里斯科歌舞厅，有两名乐队成员 [乐队成员 Gerrity 和 Broomhead] 陪同我。我离开他们去跳舞，由于我们占据的是角落的一张桌子，他们并未目睹此事。

（签名）D.M. CROWIN. 下士

由我于1957年2月22日记录。

1957年2月22日。
中尉
D.A.P.M.

pages.en:
Statements made by Mr. Mosesians (an Armenian) the manager of
the Charleston Cabaret.
No. 1.
FO - F - 1937.

I am sorry to inform you that an accident happened tonight
at 10.15 p.m. at the Charleston Cafe.

A British Soldier danced with a girl and a Italian Sailor
did the same. While dancing the Sailor pushed the Soldier.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, February 23, 1937

British, Italian
Fighters Recover

Battle In Blood Alley
Puts Cabaret Row
Out Of Bounds

As a result of a miniature war
between about 80 British soldiers
of the Loyals Regiment, and naval
ratings from the R. N. S. Lepanto,
Italian gunboat now in Harbor, in
Rue Chupaozan on Sunday even-
ing, two British tommies are de-
tained today in the Military Hos-
pital, while several others are re-
ceiving attention to their hurts.
The quarrel, which had its start
on Saturday evening, is believed
to have begun from some Tom-
mies' remarks concerning the
sportsmanship of Italian sailors
in rioting in the Isis Theatre on
Saturday afternoon.
Authorities are still making in-
vestigations, but no official state-
ments were made. Owners of the
bars and cabarets along Rue Chu-
paozan, the famed Blood Alley of
Shanghai, would make no state-
ments concerning the fight, which
started out with two soldiers and
two sailors and finally involved
about 80 men in a street fight.
Some eye-witnesses, however,
stated that the fight began in the
Charleston Cafe when an Italian
sailor and British soldier came to
blows when the sailor took the
Tommie's girl away. Reinforce-
ments were soon forthcoming, and
the fight spread to the road,
where French police and military
and naval patrols succeeded in
breaking up the fight; after one
British soldier was down with con-
cussion of the brain, and several
men of both sides suffered minor
injuries.
Today the cabarets on Rue
Chupaozan were closed to both
Loyals and Lepantos, while
doubled patrols were on watch on
Blood Alley, as investigations
were being carried out.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》（The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury），1937年2月23日，星期二

英意
斗殴者康复

血巷之战
导致歌舞厅纠纷
被列为禁区

由于周日晚上在朱葆三路（Rue Chupaozan）发生的、涉及忠诚团（Loyals Regiment）约80名英国士兵与目前停泊在港口的意大利炮舰“勒班托”号（R. N. S. Lepanto）海军士兵之间的一场小型战争，两名英国士兵今日被羁押在军医院，而其他几人正在接受伤情治疗。这场始于周六晚上的争吵，据信起因是一些英国士兵对意大利水手在周六下午伊希斯剧院（Isis Theatre）骚乱中的体育精神发表了评论。
当局仍在进行调查，但未发表官方声明。朱葆三路（上海著名的“血巷”）沿线的酒吧和歌舞厅老板拒绝就这场斗殴发表声明，该斗殴最初仅涉及两名士兵和两名水手，最终演变为约80人参与的街头斗殴。
然而，一些目击者称，斗殴始于查尔斯顿咖啡馆（Charleston Cafe），当时一名意大利水手抢走了英国士兵的女伴，双方大打出手。增援人员很快赶到，斗殴蔓延至马路上，法国警察以及军方和海军巡逻队成功驱散了斗殴人群；此时一名英国士兵因脑震荡倒地，双方均有数人受轻伤。
今日，朱葆三路上的歌舞厅禁止忠诚团士兵和“勒班托”号水手进入，同时随着调查的进行，“血巷”地区的巡逻力量加倍。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 23, 1937.

（批：19429.）
（批：A. S. B. L. 7808）

BRITISH SOLDIER
BADLY INJURED

Suffers Concussion in Fight
with Italian Sailors

NEARLY EIGHTY MEN IN
STREET AFFRAY

Two British soldiers, one with
severe concussion, were being de-
tained in the British Military Hos-
pital yesterday, while two other
soldiers and three or four Italian
naval men were injured in a fight
late Sunday evening in the Rue
Chupaozan between men of the
Loyal Regiment and naval ratings
off the Italian gunboat Lepanto. The
street in question, which is lined
with cabarets frequented with ser-
vice men, was closed to men of both
forces yesterday.

The whole affair is still the subject
of an investigation by the authorities
concerned, and no official statement
could be secured yesterday. After
sifting the various accounts of eye-
witnesses and other interested par-
ties, however, it appears that the
trouble really started on Saturday
evening, when an argument broke
out between two British soldiers and
some Italians. This was stopped by
the Military Police.

On Sunday evening, however, the
Italian seamen apparently turned up
in greater numbers. At about 10
p.m., a soldier of the Loyal Regi-
ment in the Charleston Cafe objected
to the appropriation of "his girl" by
an Italian naval rating, and an
argument ensued. Blows were ex-
changed and with men of both ser-
vices rallying to the support of their
respective men the fight became
general.

A number of chairs were broken
in the melee that ensued, and bottles
began to fly about the place, while
the cabaret girls fled; the manager
and his assistants attempted to stop
the fight, which soon spread into the
roadway. The sounds of the trouble
penetrated into the Frisco Cafe, at
the corner on the opposite side of
the road, and more men rushed into
the fray, until observers estimate
that about forty British soldiers and
a similar body of Italians were en-
gaged.

"Black-Jacks" Used?

It is alleged that the naval ratings,
ready for trouble, had armed them-
selves with "black-jacks" and pieces
of lead piping, similar to those used
in the Isis Theatre riot of the day
before, and that as a result one
British soldier was beaten so badly
about the head that he suffered a
concussion of the brain. French,
British and Italian military police
and shore patrols, reinforced by
French police constables who are al-
ways on duty nearby, managed to
separate the combatants, and within
five minutes or so the fight was over.

The injured men were taken to
hospital, three of the sailors being
later released after treatment, what
injuries were sustained by the Italian
sailors could not be learned last
night. The police area was sub-
sequently declared "out of bounds."
This order applied to all British ser-
vicemen, and a number of British
bluejackets were seen being turned
away last night by the British
Military Police.

Last night the street was quiet.
The police of all nations patrolled
the district, and there were no fur-
ther disturbances. It is understood
that the matter is being investigated
by the respective authorities, and
that steps will be taken to prevent
a recurrence of such incidents.

英国士兵
重伤

在与意大利水手的斗殴中
遭受脑震荡

近八十人参与
街头斗殴

昨日，两名英国士兵（其中一人严重脑震荡）被羁押在英国军医院，另有两名士兵和三到四名意大利海军人员在周日晚些时候于朱葆三路（Rue Chupaozan）发生的斗殴中受伤，冲突双方为忠诚团（Loyal Regiment）成员和意大利炮舰“勒班托”号（Lepanto）的海军士兵。这条街道两旁遍布服务人员常去的歌舞厅，昨日已禁止双方人员进入。

整个事件仍是有关当局调查的主题，昨日未能获得官方声明。然而，在筛选了目击者和其他相关方的各种说法后，麻烦似乎确实始于周六晚上，当时两名英国士兵与一些意大利人之间爆发了争执。此事被宪兵制止。

然而，在周日晚上，意大利水手显然以更多的人数出现。晚上约10点，查尔斯顿咖啡馆（Charleston Cafe）的一名忠诚团士兵反对一名意大利海军士兵霸占“他的女伴”，随即发生争执。双方互殴，随着两军人员纷纷支援各自的一方，斗殴演变为全面冲突。

随后的混战中，许多椅子被砸碎，瓶子开始在场所内乱飞，歌舞厅女郎四散奔逃；经理及其助手试图制止斗殴，但斗殴很快蔓延到马路上。骚乱的声音传到了马路对面拐角处的弗里斯科咖啡馆（Frisco Cafe），更多的人冲入混战，直到观察者估计约有四十名英国士兵和同样数量的意大利人参与其中。

使用了“黑杰克”（Black-Jacks，一种短棍）？

据称，蓄意滋事的海军士兵武装了自己，携带了“黑杰克”和铅管碎片，类似于前一天伊希斯剧院（Isis Theatre）骚乱中使用的那些，结果导致一名英国士兵头部遭受重创，导致脑震荡。法国、英国和意大利的宪兵及岸上巡逻队，加上附近常驻的法国巡捕增援，设法将战斗人员分开，大约五分钟后，斗殴结束。

伤者被送往医院，三名水手在接受治疗后获释，昨晚无法得知意大利水手遭受了何种伤害。随后警方将该区域宣布为“禁区”。该命令适用于所有英国服役人员，昨晚有人看到英国宪兵驱离了一些英国水兵。

昨晚街道平静。各国警察在该地区巡逻，未再发生进一步骚乱。据悉，有关当局正在调查此事，并将采取措施防止此类事件再次发生。

February 24, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

ALLEGATIONS AGAINST CHINESE WARDER NO. 97

With reference to the accident involving two motor trucks which occurred at 5.45 a.m. February 22 on Yangtsepoo Road and in which three fish hawkers were killed and four others were injured, the drivers of the two trucks named Chang Keng Foh (張根福) and Woo Shao Yuen (吳兆源) were arrested and arraigned before the Shanghai First Special District Court yesterday morning.

In requesting the Court to issue a writ of detention against the two accused, Assistant Municipal Advocate Chang Tien Ying (張天鷹) said:- "When questioned at the Police Station, the second accused, Woo Shao Yuen, driver of truck No. 16499, stated that while driving along Yangtsepoo Road he saw Chinese Warder No. 97 Hong Shuan Tsaung (項善璋) standing on the side of the road signalling his hand for the truck to stop and to give him a lift. The driver stopped his truck and this was the cause of the accident. The Chinese Warder denied the statement and is now in Court."

Chinese Warder No. 97 Hong Shuan Tsaung made the following statement in Court :- "After leaving Ward Road Gaol, I was on Yangtsepoo Road when I heard a noise of the wooden railing of the truck No. 16924 being smashed and saw a number of fish hawkers fall from the truck. I did not ask the truck No. 16499 to stop."

The first accused Chang Keng Foh, driver of the truck No. 16924, stated :- "I drove from the Fish Market with 23 fish hawkers. While passing the place of accident, the truck driven by Woo Shao Yuen suddenly overtook mine from behind and immediately afterwards it suddenly stopped. I turned my truck to the right so as to give way and while making a turn in a westerly direction, the railing on my truck broke down, throwing seven fish hawkers off the truck. The accident was due to the failure of the driver of the other truck to give a signal while stopping."

The second accused Woo Shao Yuen, who was defended by lawyer Van Kong (范剛), stated :- "I had only 8 fish hawkers on my truck. Chinese Warder No. 97 stopped me to give him a lift to Muirhead Road. I then lifted my hand as a signal to the driver of the truck behind me to stop."

Judge Hsiao Sih Feng (蕭芬) adjourned the case and ordered the two accused to be remanded in custody.

《时报》及其他本地报纸：-

针对华捕第97号的指控

关于2月22日凌晨5点45分在杨树浦路（Yangtsepoo Road）发生的涉及两辆卡车的事故，该事故造成三名鱼贩死亡，四人受伤，两辆卡车的司机张根福（Chang Keng Foh）和吴兆源（Woo Shao Yuen）已被逮捕，并于昨日上午在上海第一特区地方法院出庭受审。

在请求法院对两名被告签发拘留令时，助理市检察官张天鹰（Chang Tien Ying）表示：“在警察局受审时，第二被告、16499号卡车司机吴兆源称，他在沿杨树浦路行驶时，看到华捕第97号项善璋（Hong Shuan Tsaung）站在路边，挥手示意卡车停车并让他搭车。司机停下了卡车，这是导致事故的原因。该华捕否认了这一说法，目前正在法庭上。”

华捕第97号项善璋在法庭上作了如下陈述：“离开提篮桥监狱（Ward Road Gaol）后，我在杨树浦路上听到16924号卡车木栏杆破碎的声音，并看到数名鱼贩从卡车上摔落。我并未要求16499号卡车停车。”

第一被告、16924号卡车司机张根福称：“我载着23名鱼贩从鱼市场出发。经过事故地点时，吴兆源驾驶的卡车突然从后面超车，随后立即突然停车。我将卡车向右转以让路，在向西转弯时，我卡车上的栏杆断裂，导致七名鱼贩从卡车上摔下。事故是由于另一辆卡车司机在停车时未发出信号所致。”

第二被告吴兆源由律师范刚（Van Kong）辩护，他称：“我的卡车上只有8名鱼贩。华捕第97号拦下我，让我载他去慕尔赫德路（Muirhead Road）。随后我举手向后面的卡车司机示意停车。”

法官萧芬（Hsiao Sih Feng）宣布休庭，并命令将两名被告还押候审。
